# Contributing

Thanks for your interest in **aspose.pdf-for-go-foss** — a pure-Go,
dependency-free PDF library.

Right now the most valuable contribution is a good **bug report** — especially a
real-world PDF that the library renders, parses, or extracts incorrectly. See
[Reporting bugs](#reporting-bugs) below.

The rest of this document records the project's conventions and ground rules.
They apply to any code change and are a useful reference if you are reading the
source or proposing a fix.

## Ground rules

These are hard requirements for any change to the library:

- **Pure Go, standard library only.** The library must build with **zero
  external dependencies**. Do not add `require` entries to `go.mod`. If you need
  functionality the stdlib doesn't provide (a codec, a parser), implement it
  in-house.
- **SPDX license header.** Every `.go` file starts with the line
  `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` on its own line, a blank line, then the
  `package` declaration.
- **Mirror Aspose.PDF for .NET.** When a feature has a counterpart in
  Aspose.PDF for .NET, shape the public API after it — same concepts, type
  names, and call patterns (`Document`, `Page`, `TextFragment`, `Table`/`Row`/
  `Cell`, `BorderInfo`/`MarginInfo`, …), adapting only where Go idioms require
  it (error returns over exceptions, `io.Reader`/`io.Writer` variants, exported
  funcs over constructors). A Go developer who knows Aspose.PDF for .NET should
  recognize the API immediately.
- **Keep docs in sync.** If you change the public API, update `README.md` (and
  `CHANGELOG.md`). Code examples in the README and `examples_test.go` must
  compile.

## Development

```bash
go build ./...      # library builds (no binary — it is a library)
go test ./...       # full test suite must pass
go vet ./...        # must be clean
go run ./_examples/<name>   # run a standalone example
```

The library lives in the root package `asposepdf`. Standalone example programs
live under `_examples/<name>/main.go` (the leading `_` makes the Go toolchain
skip them in `./...`).

## Tests

- Every feature gets its own `*_test.go` file.
- Short, focused API examples go in `examples_test.go` as `ExampleXxx` functions
  with `// Output:` comments — they appear on pkg.go.dev and are validated by
  `go test`.
- Tests that need a real PDF use a file from `testdata/`, wired through the
  `testFile(t)` / `testFiles(t)` / `testGroups(t)` helpers and declared in
  `testdata/testfiles.json` (keyed by test function name). If you need a new
  test PDF, open an issue first so we can agree on the fixture.
- A bug fix should come with a regression test that fails before the fix and
  passes after.

## Reporting bugs

Open a GitHub issue with the PDF that reproduces the problem (or a minimal
synthetic one), the API call you made, what you expected, and what happened.
For rendering issues, attach the rendered output and, if you can, a reference
rendering from another viewer.

## Spec

When in doubt about PDF behavior, the normative reference is **ISO 32000-1**
(PDF 1.7) / ISO 32000-2 (PDF 2.0). Cite the relevant section in code comments
where it clarifies a non-obvious decision.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## License

This codebase is MIT-licensed (see `LICENSE` at the repo root). Every `.go` file carries an `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` header above its `package` declaration. When adding new `.go` files, preserve this convention — the header on its own line followed by a blank line, then the `package` line.

## API design

When building new functionality, always shape the public API to mirror **Aspose.PDF for .NET**. Its class/method names, types, and call patterns are the reference model: prefer the same concepts (e.g. `Document`, `Page`, `TextFragment`, `Table`/`Row`/`Cell`, `OutlineItemCollection`, `BorderInfo`/`MarginInfo`), the same method names, and the same overall workflow, adapting only where Go idioms require it (error returns instead of exceptions, `io.Reader`/`io.Writer` stream variants, exported funcs over constructors). A Go developer who knows Aspose.PDF for .NET should recognize this API immediately. When a new feature has a counterpart in Aspose.PDF for .NET, check that API first and align with it before inventing a new shape; the existing surface (noted as "Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's …" throughout the Public API section below) shows the pattern to follow.

## Commands

```bash
# Run all tests
go test ./...

# Run a single test
go test -run TestDocumentSplit ./...

# Run tests with verbose output
go test -v ./...

# Build (no binary — library only)
go build ./...
```

## Architecture

Pure Go library. No external dependencies. All PDF functionality is in the root package `asposepdf`; AI-powered operations live in the `ai` subpackage (stdlib-only too — `net/http` against OpenAI-compatible endpoints), so the root package stays free of AI and network code.

### Public API

**`document.go`** — mutable Document API; operations mutate the receiver in place
- `Open(path)` — opens a PDF file and returns a `*Document`; returns `ErrEncrypted` if the file is password-protected
- `OpenStream(r io.Reader)` — opens a PDF from an `io.Reader` and returns a `*Document`; returns `ErrEncrypted` if the file is password-protected
- `OpenWithPassword(path, password)` — opens an encrypted PDF, trying the password as both user and owner password; works on plain PDFs too
- `OpenStreamWithPassword(r io.Reader, password)` — same as `OpenWithPassword` but reads from any `io.Reader`
- `ErrEncrypted` — sentinel error returned by `Open`/`OpenStream` when the file is encrypted; check via `errors.Is(err, asposepdf.ErrEncrypted)`
- `ErrInvalidPassword` — sentinel error returned by `OpenWithPassword`/`OpenStreamWithPassword` when the password matches neither the user nor the owner password; mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `InvalidPasswordException`
- `(*Document).PageCount()` — current page count
- `(*Document).Pages()` — returns `[]*Page` live views of all pages
- `(*Document).Page(n)` — returns a `*Page` live view of page n (1-based)
- `(*Document).Rotate(angle, pageNums...) error` — rotates selected pages; rotation accumulates
- `(*Document).SetRotation(angle, pageNums...) error` — sets selected pages to exactly angle, replacing any existing rotation
- `(*Document).Reorder(order) error` — rearranges pages in place; pages may be repeated or omitted
- `(*Document).Append(others...)` — appends all pages from others into this document; nil arguments are skipped
- `(*Document).SetPassword(userPassword, ownerPassword)` — configures encryption; applied on Save/WriteTo
- `(*Document).SetPermissions(p Permissions)` — configures viewer-enforced permissions (print, copy, modify, etc.) for encrypted documents; applied on Save/WriteTo
- `(*Document).SetEncryption(opts EncryptionOptions)` — unified options-pattern API that replaces any prior encryption configuration (passwords + permissions) in one call
- `(*Document).Permissions() (Permissions, bool)` — returns the viewer permissions configured on the document; bool indicates whether the document is encrypted at all
- `(*Document).RemoveEncryption()` — clears any configured passwords and permissions so the next Save produces a plaintext PDF
- `(*Document).ChangePassword(newUserPassword, newOwnerPassword) error` — re-encrypts on the next Save with new passwords while **keeping the current algorithm and permissions** (reads them from the parsed `/Encrypt` via `preserved`, clears it, builds a fresh `encryptConfig`); the document must already be opened+decrypted (`OpenWithPassword`), empty owner defaults to the user password, errors on a plaintext document. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.ChangePasswords`
- `(*Document).WriteTo(w) (int64, error)` — writes the document to an `io.Writer` (implements `io.WriterTo`)
- `(*Document).Save(outputPath) error` — writes the document to a file
- `(*Document).Info() (DocumentInfo, error)` — returns Info-dictionary metadata read from live in-memory state; mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.Info`
- `(*Document).ExtractText(opts ...TextExtractOptions) ([]string, error)` — returns text for all pages (one entry per page); `TextExtractOptions{Mode}` selects `TextExtractReading` (visual order, default), `TextExtractRaw` (content-stream emission order) or `TextExtractFlatten` (fixed-pitch grid, positions preserved); mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `TextExtractionOptions.TextFormattingMode`
- `(*Document).ExtractTextWithLayout() ([][]TextLine, error)` — returns structured text lines for each page
- `(*Document).SearchText(query, opts...) ([]TextMatch, error)` — finds occurrences of query across all pages (each match carries its page); mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `TextFragmentAbsorber`
- `(*Document).ReplaceText(old, replacement, opts...) (int, error)` / `(*Page).ReplaceText(...)` — replaces every occurrence and returns the count; redraws the replacement at the same baseline/size/colour in a metric-compatible Standard-14 face (so any text renders even over an embedded subset font); no line re-flow; `ReplaceOptions{CaseInsensitive, Regex}`; mirrors the find-and-replace idiom of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `TextFragmentAbsorber` + `TextFragment.Text` (`replace.go`)

**`document_pages.go`** — page delete/split/extract operations
- `(*Document).DeletePage(n) error` — removes page n (1-based) in place; mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.Pages.Delete(int)`
- `(*Document).DeletePages(pageNums...) error` — removes the given 1-based pages in place; numbers are de-duplicated and validated before any removal (atomic on error); errors on no numbers or on removing every page; mirrors `Document.Pages.Delete(int[])`
- `(*Document).Split() ([]*Document, error)` — returns each page as a separate `*Document`
- `(*Document).Extract(ranges...) (*Document, error)` — returns a new `*Document` with the selected page ranges

**`form_xobject.go`** — reusable Form XObjects (ISO 32000-1 §8.10): draw content once, place it on any number of pages/positions with a single `Do`. Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `XForm`
- `(*Document).CreateForm(width, height) *XForm` — an empty Form XObject of the given size. `(*XForm).Canvas() *Page` returns the **drawing surface** — a detached page (not in `doc.pages`) on which the full `*Page` drawing API works (`AddText`, `Draw*`, `AddImage`, `AddTable`, …); `(*XForm).Size()` returns its dimensions
- `(*Page).AddForm(form *XForm, rect) error` — places the form so its `/BBox` maps onto `rect` (per-axis scale + translate via a `cm`). The `/Form` XObject is **built once on the first AddForm (frozen, `ensureBuilt`)** and reused for every later placement — one object, many `Do` invocations across pages — so finish drawing before placing. Errors on nil/cross-document form or an empty rect
- `(*Page).Forms() []*XForm` — the Form XObjects already referenced by the page (parsed from a loaded PDF, or placed earlier): each carries its existing object number + `/BBox`, so it re-places on any page of the same document with `AddForm`. `(*Document).ImportForm(form *XForm) (*XForm, error)` — copies a form **and its whole resource graph** (fonts, images, nested forms) from another document via `importGraph` (the imposition copy machinery: `collectValueDepsDoc` + `rewriteRefs`), returning a placeable XForm; a same-document form is returned unchanged
- Mechanism: `Page` gained an optional `obj *pdfObject` override so `pageObj()` can target a detached canvas dict without polluting `doc.pages`; `CreateForm` makes such a canvas, drawing appends to its `/Contents` + `/Resources` like any page, and `build()` harvests them into `makeFormXObjectWithResources`. Placement reuses `registerFormXObject` (`/Fm0`, `/Fm1`, … in the page `/Resources/XObject`); `bboxFromForm` reads a parsed form's `/BBox`. Out of scope: in-place editing of a parsed form's content stream

**`imposition.go`** — N-up / booklet page imposition (returns a new `*Document`; receiver untouched). A **production helper, not an ISO 32000 feature** — built from spec primitives (each source page wrapped in a Form XObject §8.10, placed via a `cm` transform), so the output is an ordinary, spec-compliant PDF. Mirrors the *intent* of Aspose.PDF for .NET's legacy `PdfFileEditor.MakeNUp`/`MakeBooklet`, but follows this library's `Document`-method paradigm rather than the file-path facade shape
- `(*Document).NUp(opts NUpOptions) (*Document, error)` — imposes pages onto larger sheets in a `Rows`×`Cols` grid; each source page is scaled to fit its cell preserving aspect ratio and centered; sheets fill until all pages placed (last sheet may have empty cells)
- `NUpOptions` struct — `Rows, Cols int` (≥1), `PageSize PageFormat` (zero → A4), `Margin float64`, `Gutter float64`, `Order NUpOrder`, `DrawBorder bool`
- `NUpOrder` enum — `NUpRowMajor` (default), `NUpColumnMajor`
- `(*Document).Booklet(opts BookletOptions) (*Document, error)` — imposes pages two-up reordered for saddle-stitch (print double-sided, fold, read in order); page count padded up to a multiple of 4 with blank halves
- `BookletOptions` struct — `PageSize PageFormat` (zero → `2·W × H` of the first page, i.e. source pages at 100%), `Binding BookletBinding`
- `BookletBinding` enum — `BindingLeft` (default, LTR), `BindingRight` (RTL, mirrors each spread)
- Internals: `importPageAsXObject` wraps a page (content + `/Resources`) as a `/Subtype /Form` XObject with `/BBox` = MediaBox; `importGraph` copies each page's resource graph into the result once (shared objects deduped via a single `idMap`, reusing `collectValueDepsDoc` + `rewriteRefs`); `makePlacement` computes the fit-inside `cm`; `addImposedSheet` emits `q cm /Xn Do Q` per cell. Known limits (v1): inherited `/Resources` from the page-tree parent not resolved (uses the page dict's own `/Resources`); no creep/shingling

**`page.go`** — `RotationAngle` type and constants (`Rotate0`, `Rotate90`, `Rotate180`, `Rotate270`)

**`page.go`** — Page and PageSize types
- `PageSizes(inputPath)` — returns dimensions of every page in a PDF file
- `(*Page).Number()` — 1-based page number within the document
- `(*Page).Size() (PageSize, error)` — page dimensions (width/height) from MediaBox (with inheritance from page tree)
- `(*Page).Rotation()` — effective rotation in degrees (0, 90, 180, 270); reflects Document.Rotate patches
- `(*Page).MediaBox() (Rectangle, error)` — full page rectangle (with inheritance); mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Page.MediaBox`
- `(*Page).CropBox() (Rectangle, error)` — visible region as a `Rectangle`; falls back to MediaBox if not set
- `(*Page).TrimBox() (Rectangle, error)` — intended trim dimensions; falls back to CropBox then MediaBox
- `(*Page).BleedBox() (Rectangle, error)` — production bleed region; falls back to CropBox then MediaBox
- `(*Page).ArtBox() (Rectangle, error)` — meaningful content extent; falls back to CropBox then MediaBox
- `(*Page).SetMediaBox/SetCropBox/SetTrimBox/SetBleedBox/SetArtBox(Rectangle) error` — set the respective box directly on the page (validated, overrides inherited/referenced values); mirror Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Page.*Box` setters
- `(*Page).SetPageSize(width, height float64) error` — resize the page by setting its MediaBox to `[0 0 width height]` (content is not scaled); mirrors `Page.SetPageSize`
- `(*Page).ExtractText(opts ...TextExtractOptions) (string, error)` — returns the text content of a page in visual reading order (default), raw emission order (`TextExtractRaw`) or laid out on a fixed-pitch grid (`TextExtractFlatten`); unknown font characters become U+FFFD. `TextExtractionMode` enum: `TextExtractReading`, `TextExtractRaw`, `TextExtractFlatten`
- **Flattened layout** (`buildFlattenedTextFromFragments`, `text_layout.go`, `pdf-go-r30a`): each fragment starts at the column its x position maps to, the space between fragments is padding, and a vertical gap wider than 1.5 line heights becomes a blank line — so the output reads like the page in a monospace font, columns stay columns without a table detector, and two revisions of a page diff cleanly. The cell width is the **median** advance per character on the page (the median, not the minimum, so one narrow superscript cannot stretch the page into ribbons); the origin is the leftmost text, so the left column starts at 0 regardless of the page margin. A fragment whose column falls behind text already placed is separated by a single space instead of overwriting it. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `TextFormattingMode.Flatten`
- `(*Page).ExtractTextWithLayout() ([]TextLine, error)` — returns structured text lines in visual reading order with coordinates and font info
- `(*Page).Paragraphs() (PageMarkup, error)` / `(*Document).Paragraphs() ([]PageMarkup, error)` (`paragraph.go`) — **structural extraction**: groups a page's text into columns (`MarkupSection`) and paragraphs (`MarkupParagraph{Text, Rectangle, Lines}`). Built on the `ExtractTextWithLayout` pipeline: fragments are clustered into columns by a horizontal occupancy histogram (a wide vertical gutter with text on both sides splits columns), then each column's lines are grouped into paragraphs by the vertical gap between baselines and font-size changes. Heuristic (figures/tables may split/merge); recovers prose paragraph/column structure well. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `ParagraphAbsorber` (`PageMarkup → MarkupSection → MarkupParagraph`)
- `(*Page).SearchText(query string, opts ...SearchOptions) ([]TextMatch, error)` — finds occurrences of query on the page in reading order, returning a bounding `Rectangle` per match (`text_search.go`); built on the layout pipeline, matches are located within a single line; literal by default, with optional case-insensitive and RE2-regex modes. Match rectangles use the per-glyph start positions recorded during extraction (`textFragment.runeX` → unexported `TextFragment.runeX`), so sub-fragment boxes are accurate rather than interpolated (right edge approximate only when a match ends a fragment's last glyph). Vertically a match rectangle is the **text box**, descender to ascender (`matchRect`: `Y + descent` .. `+ Height`, with the unexported `TextFragment.descent` carried from extraction), the convention viewers use for highlight and redaction quads (`pdf-go-7lkk`); non-embedded Standard-14 fonts, which have no `/FontDescriptor`, take their ascender/descender from the AFM (`standard14VerticalMetrics`, aliases like Arial included), so their fragment `Height` is the real text box rather than the whole em
- `SearchOptions` struct — CaseInsensitive bool, Regex bool, Rectangle *Rectangle (non-nil limits results to matches whose box intersects the region, per page; mirrors Aspose's `TextSearchOptions.Rectangle`), SearchInAnnotations bool (also matches annotation `/Contents` text — sticky notes, free text, markup — each match's `Rect` is the annotation rectangle; mirrors Aspose's `TextSearchOptions.SearchInAnnotations`). Zero value = case-sensitive literal, whole-page, page-content only, matching Aspose.PDF for .NET's default
- `TextMatch` struct — Text string, PageNumber int (1-based), Rect Rectangle (PDF user space)
- `PageSize` struct — Width, Height in points (1/72 inch)
- `Color` struct — R, G, B, A float64 (values in [0, 1])
- `TextLine` struct — Text, Y, Fragments []TextFragment
- `TextFragment` struct — Text, X, Y, Width, FontName, FontSize, Height, Bold, Italic, CharSpacing, Color Color, IsSubscript, IsSuperscript, Rotation (baseline angle in degrees CCW from the combined text matrix; rotated fragments are isolated into their own TextLines, never merged into horizontal lines; HTML export emits transform:rotate, Markdown export drops all-rotated paragraphs as decoration)
- `(*Page).ExtractImages() ([]Image, error)` — returns all images found on the page
- `(*Document).ExtractImages() ([][]Image, error)` — returns images for all pages (one slice per page)
- `Image` struct — Data, Format, Width, Height, BPC, ColorSpace, X, Y, PageWidth, PageHeight, Inline
- `ImageFormat` — ImageFormatPNG, ImageFormatJPEG
- `ImageColorSpace` — ColorSpaceDeviceRGB, ColorSpaceDeviceGray, ColorSpaceDeviceCMYK, ColorSpaceIndexed, ColorSpaceICCBased
- `(*Image).Save(path) error` — writes the image data to a file
- `(*Image).WriteTo(w) (int64, error)` — writes the image data to a writer
- `ImageInfo` struct — Width, Height, BPC, ColorSpace, Format, X, Y, PageWidth, PageHeight, Inline, Name
- `(*ImageInfo).Extract() (*Image, error)` — decodes the image and returns the full Image with pixel data
- `(*Page).ImageInfos() ([]ImageInfo, error)` — returns metadata for all images without decoding
- `(*Document).ImageInfos() ([][]ImageInfo, error)` — returns image metadata for all pages without decoding
- `(*ImageInfo).Replace(path) error` — replaces image data from a file; format detected by magic bytes (JPEG, PNG); position unchanged
- `(*ImageInfo).ReplaceFromStream(r) error` — replaces image data from an io.Reader
- `(*ImageInfo).Remove() error` — removes image from page (resources + content stream); XObject stays in doc objects
- `Rectangle` struct — LLX, LLY, URX, URY (PDF rectangle in points)
- `(*Page).AddImage(path, rect) error` — adds an image from a file to the page; format detected by magic bytes (JPEG, PNG)
- `(*Page).AddImageFromStream(r, rect) error` — adds an image from an io.Reader to the page
- `(*Page).AddInlineImage(path, rect) error` / `(*Page).AddInlineImageFromStream(r, rect) error` — draws a small image **inline** in the content stream (`BI … ID … EI`, ISO 32000-1 §8.9.7) instead of as an Image XObject; for tiny one-off pictures (icons, rules). PNG and JPEG inputs; both are decoded to 8-bpc samples and re-stored as Flate, then ASCIIHex-wrapped (`/F [/AHx /Fl]`) so the `EI` boundary is unambiguous (the `>` EOD never recurs in hex — a binary or ASCII85 stream can contain a spurious `>EI`). PNG alpha is flattened over white (inline images cannot carry a soft mask). `AddImage` (an XObject) stays the recommended default for anything but tiny images (`image_inline_write.go`)
- `ImageToDocument(path, opts...) (*Document, error)` — creates a single-page PDF from an image file; DPI-aware page sizing
- `ImageToDocumentFromStream(r, opts...) (*Document, error)` — creates a single-page PDF from an image reader
- `ImageToDocumentOptions` struct — PageWidth, PageHeight, MarginLeft, MarginRight, MarginTop, MarginBottom
- `(*Document).RemoveUnusedObjects() int` — removes objects not reachable from any page or from the document catalog (`/Root` is a GC root too, so `/Metadata`, `/OutputIntents`, `/AcroForm`, `/StructTreeRoot`, `/Names`, etc. are never dropped just because no page also references them); entries the writer rebuilds are not followed (`catalogKeyRebuiltByWriter`: `/Pages` always, `/Outlines` once the tree is loaded via `Outlines()`), nor is a page's own `/Parent` (`collectReachableIDs`) — on a reopened file the old page-tree number is free and the next new object takes it, which would otherwise keep that object alive forever; returns count of removed objects
- `OptimizeImageOptions` struct — MaxDPI, JPEGQuality, ConvertPNGToJPEG
- `(*Document).OptimizeImages(opts) (int, error)` — optimizes images to reduce file size; downscales above MaxDPI, converts opaque PNG to JPEG
- `(*Document).Optimize(OptimizationOptions) (OptimizationResult, error)` (`optimize.go`) — unified size-reduction pass mirroring Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.OptimizeResources(OptimizationOptions)`. Folds `RemoveUnusedObjects`/`OptimizeImages`/`SubsetFonts` and adds three lossless transforms, run in order images→fonts→compress→dedupe→remove-unused→compress-objects. `OptimizationOptions{RemoveUnusedObjects, SubsetFonts, CompressStreams, RemoveDuplicateStreams, CompressObjects, Images *OptimizeImageOptions}`; `DefaultOptimizationOptions()` is the safe lossless preset (all on, including object-stream packing, except image recompression, which is opt-in via `Images` because it can be lossy). `OptimizationResult` reports per-op counts, including `CompressedObjects` (objects eligible for packing; the packing itself happens on Save/WriteTo). **`compressUncompressedStreams`**: marks source streams stored without a `/Filter` (`Decoded=false`) as decoded so the writer Flate-compresses them (skips `/Type /Metadata` — PDF/A wants it raw — image XObjects, and streams < 48 bytes). **`removeDuplicateStreams`**: hashes each stream (`streamSignature` = sha256 of `canonicalDict` sans `/Length` + `decodedStreamData`), merges byte-identical stream objects into the lowest-numbered keeper, and repoints every reference — including refs embedded in content-stream bytes — via `rewriteRefs`; limitation: dicts must be literally equal (a producer that cloned a subtree with fresh object numbers isn't deduped). **`CompressObjects`** (in the default preset, `objstm_write.go`, `pdf-go-o0wy`): `Optimize` sets `Document.compressObjects`, and `buildDocumentPDF` branches to `buildObjectStreamPDF`, which writes ineligible objects as ordinary indirect objects, every other object in Flate-compressed `/ObjStm` streams of up to 100 (`objStmCapacity`), and a `/Type /XRef` cross-reference stream instead of the classic table (header raised to at least `%PDF-1.5`). Never packed (`objectPackable`): streams, the encryption dictionary, signature dictionaries (their placeholders are patched by byte offset). A packed object is written without per-object encryption — the object stream is encrypted as a stream under its own number — and the cross-reference stream is never encrypted. `appendRevision` writes a cross-reference stream section (`encodeRevisionXRef`, `/Index` subsections + `/Prev`) when the file's last section is one, so incremental signing and `AddValidationInfo` keep the file's kind. The flag lives on the in-memory document only (reopening a compressed file and saving writes classic unless `Optimize` runs again) and `SaveLinearized` ignores it. **PDF/A-1 guard**: PDF/A-1 is PDF 1.4-based, where neither object nor cross-reference streams are allowed, so `buildDocumentPDF` takes the object-stream branch only when the document's own XMP does not identify it as PDF/A-1 (`isPDFA1`, `validate_pdfa.go` — `pdfaid:part` read via the same regex `ValidatePDFA` uses). Checking at write time, not just the flag, covers every call order — `ConvertToPDFA(PDFA1B)` followed by `Optimize(DefaultOptimizationOptions())` still writes classic — and a document opened from an existing PDF/A-1 file whose XMP was never touched by `ConvertToPDFA` at all. `ConvertToPDFA` also clears `compressObjects` for PDF/A-1 formats as a convenience, but the writer-side check is what actually enforces it. Corpus: 1003 documents resaved compressed, qpdf's syntax check found no problems introduced by the packing (16 problems found were pre-existing in the source files), 21.6% smaller than the classic save. **`UnembedFonts`** (`font_unembed.go`, `pdf-go-vb4b`, opt-in — not in `DefaultOptimizationOptions`, since unlike every other transform here it can change how the document actually looks): drops the embedded program from a simple (Type1/TrueType/MMType1) font whose `/BaseFont` and `/Widths` are both metric-compatible with a Helvetica/Times/Courier Standard-14 face — `unembedTargetName` recognizes the literal 12 non-symbolic Standard-14 names plus the same Arial/Times New Roman/Courier New aliasing `standard14WidthAlias` already does for the read side (`font_metrics.go`), deliberately excluding Symbol/ZapfDingbats (Standard-14 names too, but with no metric-compatible substitute — `render_std14.go` — so removing their program would leave the text unrenderable, not merely reshaped); `unembedWidthsMatch` then checks every code's own `/Widths` entry against the target's AFM table (±1/1000 em) so a font that merely happens to share a common name (a mislabeled or customized face) isn't unembedded on name alone. Only the font-program keys (`/FontFile*`, `/Length1-3`) are stripped from `/FontDescriptor` — `/Widths`/`/Encoding`/`/BaseFont` are untouched, so layout is provably unaffected (advance widths never depended on whether the program was embedded) and only glyph shapes can differ, in a viewer whose installed/bundled substitute doesn't exactly match. Composite (Type0/CID) and Type3 fonts are out of scope (Standard-14 is Latin-only, so there's no substitute story for a CID-keyed font). Orphaned `/FontFile*` stream objects are left for the caller's `RemoveUnusedObjects` pass, same as every other `Optimize` transform
- `(*Document).ConvertToGrayscale() error` (`grayscale.go`) — converts the whole document to grayscale in place by mapping every colour to its luminance grey (`0.3R+0.59G+0.11B`; CMYK via CMYK→RGB→luminance). Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `RgbToDeviceGrayConversionStrategy`. Coverage: content-stream device colours (`rg`/`RG`/`k`/`K`→`g`/`G`, and `sc`/`scn` when the active `cs`/`CS` space — tracked + resolved from `/Resources/ColorSpace` — is DeviceRGB/Gray/CMYK or ICCBased N=1/3/4, converted to equal-channel grey in place); raster images (decoded via the existing image pipeline, re-encoded as 8-bpc `/DeviceGray`, `/SMask` preserved, `/ImageMask` stencils left to the greyed fill colour); axial/radial (type 2/3) shadings + shading patterns (greys the function `/C0`/`/C1` and `/Background`, sets `/ColorSpace /DeviceGray`); tiling patterns (recursed); and annotation `/C`/`/IC`/`/MK` colours + `/AP` appearance streams — recursing through Form XObjects (each content/image stream processed once via visited-sets). Best-effort / left unconverted (documented): Separation/DeviceN tints, Pattern-name fills, Indexed palettes, and type 0/4 shading functions. Content is rewritten with `serializeContentOps` into a single fresh `/Contents` stream
- `(*Document).FlattenTransparency(opts ...FlattenTransparencyOptions) (int, error)` (`flatten_transparency.go`, `pdf-go-bqxs`) — eliminates transparency in place; needed because PDF/A-1 (ISO 19005-1) forbids it entirely (`ValidatePDFA`'s `TRANSPARENCY` issue, PDF/A-1 only — `pdfaCheckTransparency`/`pdfaDictHasTransparency` in validate_pdfa.go, reused here as-is). Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.FlattenTransparency()`. Scope (v1): **whole-page rasterization** — a page whose `/Resources` graph (walked recursively through Form XObjects/Patterns via `collectValueDepsDoc`, same as imposition's resource-copy machinery) or own `/Group` carries a transparency group, `/SMask`, a non-Normal blend mode, or `/ca`/`/CA` < 1 is rendered to an opaque raster and its `/Contents` replaced with a single full-page image; a page without any of those is left completely untouched (still vector, still searchable). Not a sub-region approach (render only the transparent bit, splice it in, leave the rest of the page as-is) — rejected because nothing in the renderer separates a transparency region's ops from surrounding vector ops in z-order; see the design doc for the full reasoning. Out of scope: annotation-level transparency (own opacity, or transparency inside `/AP`) — detection only walks page content + `/Resources`, not `/Annots`, so annotations keep rendering live unchanged; call `Annotation.Flatten()`/`Form.Flatten()` first to bake those into page content (where this pass then does catch them) if that's also needed. `FlattenTransparencyOptions{DPI, Pages}` (DPI 0 → `DefaultDPI`; Pages empty → every page). Mechanics: `renderContentForFlatten` rasterizes content only (a new `skipAnnotations` renderer flag, alongside `suppressText`/`hideFormWidgets`) in the page's own **unrotated** coordinate space — `RenderImage` bakes `/Rotate` into its output for direct display, but a raster placed back via `cm`+`Do` must not have rotation baked in twice, since the page's untouched `/Rotate` still applies once at display time (regression-tested, `TestFlattenTransparencyPreservesRotation`: rotation applied exactly once, not zero or twice — a small tolerance, not exact byte equality, since `deviceMatrix` rounds the embed-time pixel dimensions and the image is then rescaled to the box's exact point dimensions on redisplay, causing a fraction of a percent of ordinary sub-pixel resampling noise at content edges, same as any rasterize-then-redisplay pipeline). The image is PNG-encoded (always opaque by construction, so Go's encoder drops the alpha channel and no `/SMask` is reintroduced) and its registration into a fresh `/Resources` is fully prepared — including via `createImageXObject`, the same helper `AddImage` uses — before the page dict is touched at all, so a failure partway through never leaves `/Resources` wiped with `/Contents` still pointing at names that no longer exist; `replacePageContents` (shared with the redaction pipeline) then swaps in one new `/Contents` stream, and any page-level `/Group` is deleted (its content has been rasterized away — code review caught an earlier version that detected a page-level group but never cleared it, so `ValidatePDFA` kept flagging `TRANSPARENCY` and a second `FlattenTransparency` call kept re-flattening the same page forever; `TestFlattenTransparencyClearsPageGroup` regression-tests both). Calls `RemoveUnusedObjects` once at the end when it flattened at least one page — found necessary during testing: `pdfaCheckTransparency` scans every object in the document, not just reachable ones, so an orphaned ExtGState left behind by a flattened page would still trip `TRANSPARENCY` otherwise. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-flatten-transparency-design.md`

Implementation (`font_subset.go`): tracks used glyph IDs as the text encoders emit them, takes the transitive closure over composite-glyph components, renumbers the kept glyphs into a compact range, rebuilds `glyf`/`loca`/`hmtx`/`maxp`/`head`/`hhea` + a synthetic `post` 3.0 (drops `cmap`/`OS/2`/`name`/hinting), and reassembles the sfnt with correct checksums. - `(*Page).AddText(text, style, rect) error` — draws text inside a rectangle with word wrap, alignment, clipping, optional underline/strikethrough, rotation, and behind-content mode. **RTL / bidirectional** (`bidi.go`, epic `pdf-go-emak` phase 1): when the text is `TextStyle.RTL` or contains any strong right-to-left character, each wrapped line is reordered into visual order by a pragmatic Unicode Bidi Algorithm (UAX #9: classes W1–W7 / N1–N2 / I1–I2 over a single line, L2 reordering, L4 mirroring) before glyph emission, and an RTL base paragraph defaults to right alignment. This runs entirely in the layout layer — the encoder and renderer are untouched. **Arabic contextual shaping** (`arabic_shape.go`, phase 2) runs first, on the logical string: `shapeArabic` maps each letter to its Unicode Presentation Forms-B glyph (isolated / initial / medial / final by joining context) and forms the mandatory lam-alef ligatures, so a font that covers Forms-B (e.g. DejaVu Sans) renders connected Arabic. Hebrew and Arabic both render correctly (verified visually: connected Arabic, right-aligned, with numbers kept LTR). Out of scope for the bidi layer: explicit embedding/isolate codes, the bracket-pair rule N0, the L1 trailing-whitespace reset. **OpenType shaping** (`opentype.go` / `shape.go` / `text_shape.go` / `combining.go` / `arabic_joining.go` / `normalize_data.go`, phase 3, epic `pdf-go-26u4`; spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-opentype-shaping-design.md`): an embedded font (`LoadFont`) carrying GSUB/GPOS is shaped by a pure-Go OpenType engine. The reader (`parseOTLayout`, lazily cached as `ttfFont.layout()`) reads GDEF (glyph classes, mark attachment classes, mark glyph sets), GSUB types 1–8 and GPOS types 1–9 (extensions resolved at parse time) defensively — a malformed subtable is dropped, never fatal; lookup types/subtable counts/features/scripts match fontTools on DejaVu, Amiri, Noto Naskh and Noto Sans Arabic. The engine (`shapeRun`) follows HarfBuzz: a logical-order buffer, per-glyph feature masks, lookups applied in lookup-list order, LookupFlag + GDEF + mark-filtering-set skipping (`otMatcher`), one context/chain-context matcher for GSUB 5/6 and GPOS 7/8 with nested-lookup position bookkeeping (`applyNested`), ligature component tracking for mark-to-ligature, and cursive/mark attachment recorded as chains then resolved into absolute offsets (`resolveAttachments`, direction-aware advance compensation). Per run: `normalizeForFont` decomposes characters the font lacks, puts marks in canonical order using HarfBuzz's modified Hebrew/Arabic classes (dagesh before vowels, shadda before fatha) and recomposes what the font has (UCD tables generated into `combining.go` / `normalize_data.go`); Arabic joining masks come from the UCD joining types (`arabic_joining.go`, so Persian/Urdu/Syriac/N'Ko letters join); feature plans are Arabic `ccmp locl isol init medi fina med2 fin2 fin3 rlig rclt calt liga mset` + `curs kern dist abvm blwm mark mkmk`, default `ccmp locl liga clig calt rclt rlig` + `kern dist abvm blwm mark mkmk`; default-ignorable characters end as zero-advance space glyphs. **Glyph-for-glyph identical to HarfBuzz** (uharfbuzz) on a 54-string Arabic/Persian/Urdu/Hebrew/Latin differential suite across those four fonts. Wiring in `renderTextInBuilder`: wrapping stays rune-based; each wrapped line is split into bidi level runs (`bidiLevelRuns`, RTL runs mirrored), each run shaped in logical order and reversed, and `shapedLine.showOps` emits a plain `Tj` when the shaped positions agree with the font's rounded `/W` widths (sub-thousandth residuals are carried, so unkerned text is byte-identical to the old path), `TJ` kerning numbers where they differ, and `Ts` text rise around off-baseline marks. The Forms-B pass is skipped when the font's GSUB shapes Arabic itself (`fontShapesArabic`). **Shaped text stays extractable**: a substituted glyph claims a `/ToUnicode` entry for its text (`embeddedFont.claimGlyphText` — ligatures and contextual forms, allowed to override presentation-form code points such as U+FB03; folded in before serialization by `refreshShapedText` in `assemble` and by `SubsetFonts`), while glyphs that cannot carry their text through `/ToUnicode` — a glyph already nominal for another character (Noto Naskh draws zain as its reh glyph plus a dot), decomposition pieces with no character of their own, hidden joiners — are wrapped in `/Span <</ActualText …>> BDC … EMC`. MuPDF renders of Amiri/Noto/DejaVu samples match ours, and the showcase's RTL block is pixel-identical before and after. Fonts without layout tables, Standard-14 and Type3 fonts keep the rune-by-rune path. Out of scope: the Indic/Khmer/Myanmar/Hangul reordering shapers, vertical text, alternate-glyph selection, device/variation tables

**`encrypt.go` / `decrypt.go` / `encrypt_aes.go` / `decrypt_aes.go` / `encrypt_aes256.go` / `decrypt_aes256.go`**
- `Encrypt(inputPath, outputPath, userPassword, ownerPassword)` — top-level helper writes RC4-128-protected PDF (PDF 1.4 Standard Security Handler V=2 R=3). For AES, use `(*Document).SetEncryption(EncryptionOptions{...})`
- `ErrEncrypted` — sentinel error from `Open`/`OpenStream` on encrypted input
- `ErrInvalidPassword` — sentinel error from `OpenWithPassword`/`OpenStreamWithPassword` on a password matching neither `/U` nor `/O`. A decryption-setup failure is final in `openStreamCore` (wrapped as `encryptionSetupError`): xref reconstruction is never retried after one, and a reconstructed trailer carries `/Encrypt` from the primary trailer, the last `/XRef` stream, or a scanned security-handler dict, so an encrypted file never opens as plain
- Decryption pipeline: `OpenWithPassword`/`OpenStreamWithPassword` parse `/Encrypt`, dispatch by `/V` (V=2 R=3 → RC4 path; V=4 R=4 → AES-128 path via `/CFM /AESV2`; V=5 R=6 → AES-256 path via `/CFM /AESV3` per ISO 32000-2; V=5 R=5, the Adobe Extension Level 3 predecessor, → the same path, read-only). All paths share PKCS#7 helpers. For V≤4 password handling reuses Algorithms 2/5/7 (MD5-based); for V=5 R=6 password handling uses Algorithm 2.B (iterated SHA-256/384/512 hash chain), for R=5 a single SHA-256 (`hashV5R5`, selected by `hashV5`). `encryptState.revision` records R=5 so a preserved re-save writes `/R 5` back (and omits `/Perms` if the file had none); any explicit password change re-encrypts as R=6. Per-object decryption uses Algorithm 1 (RC4) or 1.A (AES-128, with `"sAlT"` literal suffix in MD5 input); AES-256 uses the FEK directly (no per-object derivation). Stream `/Filter` chains are re-applied after decryption per PDF spec ordering (encrypt-after-filter)
- `Permissions` struct — eight bool flags (AllowPrint, AllowModify, AllowCopy, AllowAnnotations, AllowFormFill, AllowAccessibility, AllowAssembly, AllowPrintHighRes); zero value denies everything. Adobe-convention bit packing per ISO 32000-1 §7.6.3.2 Table 22 with reserved bits 7-8 and 13-32 set high
- `EncryptionOptions` struct — unified encryption configuration: UserPassword, OwnerPassword (empty → defaults to UserPassword), Permissions *Permissions (nil → grant all), Algorithm EncryptionAlgorithm (zero value → AES-128). Consumed by `(*Document).SetEncryption`
- `EncryptionAlgorithm` enum — `EncryptionAlgAES128` (default, AES-128 V=4 R=4 `/CFM /AESV2` per ISO 32000-1 §7.6.3.2), `EncryptionAlgRC4_128` (legacy V=2 R=3), `EncryptionAlgRC4_40` (the original handler V=1 R=2, `/Length 40`, `pdf-go-aqux` — for old readers and archives only: a 40-bit key falls to brute force in minutes; the revision-2 forms of Algorithms 2/3/4 were already implemented for *reading* such files, so writing them reuses them), `EncryptionAlgAES256` (AES-256 V=5 R=6 `/CFM /AESV3` per ISO 32000-2 §7.6.4; bumps PDF header to `%PDF-2.0` and includes /U /O /UE /OE /Perms entries with tamper-detection)
- AES-128 specifics: per-object key via `MD5(docKey || objNum_LE_3 || gen_LE_2 || "sAlT")[:16]` (Algorithm 1.A); AES-128-CBC with PKCS#7 padding and random 16-byte IV prepended to each encrypted string/stream. Single document-wide StdCF crypt filter; `/StmF` and `/StrF` both point to it
- **No `usePdf20` toggle.** Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Encrypt(..., bool usePdf20)` chooses between revision 5 (the deprecated Adobe extension) and revision 6 (ISO 32000-2). This library always writes R=6 for AES-256, so the flag could only select the weaker, withdrawn revision — it is deliberately absent (`pdf-go-aqux`)
- AES-256 specifics: random 256-bit File Encryption Key (FEK) is encrypted into /UE under user-derived key and /OE under owner-derived key; passwords are validated against /U / /O hashes computed by Algorithm 2.B; /Perms is an AES-256-ECB encrypted permissions block under FEK providing tamper-detection of /P. Per-object encryption uses FEK directly with AES-256-CBC + PKCS#7 + random 16-byte IV. PDF header bumped to `%PDF-2.0` per ISO 32000-2 requirement

**`pubsec.go`** — public-key security handler (ISO 32000-1 §7.6.4, `/Filter /Adobe.PubSec`; epic `pdf-go-dn5`): encrypt for X.509 recipients instead of a shared password. Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's certificate encryption, in this library's options idiom
- `EncryptionOptions.Recipients []Recipient` (`Recipient{Certificate *x509.Certificate, Permissions *Permissions}`) switches `SetEncryption` to the public-key handler and defaults the algorithm to AES-256; `OpenWithCertificate(path, cert, key)` / `OpenStreamWithCertificate(r, cert, key)` open such a file, taking any `crypto.Decrypter` (an `*rsa.PrivateKey` satisfies it — no `.p12` needed), the read-side counterpart of `Sign`'s `crypto.Signer`
- Mechanics: a random 20-byte seed plus that recipient's 4 permission bytes (`pubsecPermissionBits` — bit 1 set, bits 7-8 clear, 13-32 set, the Acrobat/PDFBox convention) are sealed per recipient into a CMS EnvelopedData (`buildRecipientEnvelope`: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 key transport + AES-CBC content encryption, hand-rolled on `encoding/asn1` next to the SignedData code, reusing `algorithmIdentifier`/`issuerAndSerial`/`contentInfo`). The **file key** is the digest of the seed followed by every recipient blob in `/Recipients` order — SHA-256 for AESV3, SHA-1 for AESV2 (`pubsecFileKey`) — so any recipient who recovers the seed derives the same key. Per-object encryption/decryption is then the unchanged standard-handler machinery, which is why the whole read/write pipeline is shared
- `/Encrypt` layout: `/Filter /Adobe.PubSec`, `/SubFilter /adbe.pkcs7.s5`, `/V 4` (AESV2) or `/V 5` (AESV3), no `/O` `/U` `/P` (permissions live in the envelopes), and `/Recipients` inside the `/DefaultCryptFilter` crypt filter; the reader also accepts `/Recipients` on the encryption dict itself and any crypt-filter name
- **Per-recipient permissions** are a genuine capability gain over the password handler; `Permissions()` reports the ones from the caller's own envelope. Opening a certificate-encrypted file re-saves for the same recipients (the parsed state is preserved verbatim), so edit-in-place works
- Validated: **OpenSSL** (`cms -decrypt -recip cert.pem -inkey key.pem`) recovers the payload byte-for-byte from our envelope; unit tests cover AES-128/AES-256 round-trip, multi-recipient, non-recipient and wrong-key rejection, per-recipient permissions and re-save. Out of scope: RC4 sub-filters s3/s4, EC recipients (key agreement), and RSAES-OAEP key transport

**`sign.go` / `pkcs7_sign.go` / `pkcs7_timestamp.go` / `sign_incremental.go` / `sign_verify.go` / `pkcs7_verify.go` / `appearance_sign.go`** — digital signatures (ISO 32000-1 §12.8; epic `pdf-go-bm9`). PKCS#7-detached signatures (`/adbe.pkcs7.detached` or PAdES `/ETSI.CAdES.detached`), SHA-2 or SHA-3 digests, RSA or ECDSA keys, over plain **or encrypted** documents; invisible by default or a visible appearance block; optional certification (DocMDP), RFC 3161 trusted timestamp, and **multiple signatures** via incremental update. Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `PdfFileSignature` + `SignatureCustomAppearance`
- `(*Document).Sign(opts SignOptions) error` — configures a signature applied on the next Save/WriteTo (like `SetEncryption`). `SignOptions` — `Certificate *x509.Certificate`, `PrivateKey crypto.Signer` (RSA/ECDSA — no `.p12` file needed; caller loads the key however) or `SignHash` for a key the process never sees, `Chain []*x509.Certificate`, `Reason`/`Location`/`ContactInfo`/`Name`, `SigningTime`. Signing an encrypted document is rejected
- `SignOptions.SignHash func(digest []byte, hash crypto.Hash) ([]byte, error)` (`pdf-go-7p2n`) — sign without holding the key: the callback is handed the digest and the hash that produced it and returns the raw signature (PKCS#1 v1.5 for an RSA certificate, ASN.1 ECDSA for an EC one), which is the shape a hardware module or a remote signing service offers. Internally it is wrapped in a `crypto.Signer` (`callbackSigner`, `Public()` answering from the certificate), so the CMS path stays single. Exactly one of `PrivateKey` and `SignHash` must be set and `Certificate` is required either way — the `SignerInfo` is built from it. A callback error surfaces from `Save`/`WriteTo` rather than producing a broken file. Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `CustomSignHash`
- `SignOptions.Digest DigestAlgorithm` — the hash for the message digest and the signature: `DigestSHA256` (zero value, what every earlier release wrote), `DigestSHA384`, `DigestSHA512`, `DigestSHA3_256`, `DigestSHA3_384`, `DigestSHA3_512`. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `DigestHashAlgorithm`. SHA-3 comes from the standard library (`crypto/sha3`, blank-imported so the hashes register); the OID tables live in `pkcs7_sign.go` — digests under the NIST hashAlgs arc, and for the signature algorithm bare `rsaEncryption` with a SHA-2 digest (the long-proven form) but the explicit `id-rsassa-pkcs1-v1_5-with-sha3-*` / `id-ecdsa-with-sha3-*` identifiers for SHA-3, which not every validator recognises in the rsaEncryption pairing. ECDSA now names its digest correctly too (`ecdsa-with-SHA384/512`), where it used to write SHA-256 whatever the hash. The verifier reads the algorithm from the `SignerInfo` rather than assuming, so a SHA-3 signature round-trips. Validated with **OpenSSL** (`cms -verify` accepts our SHA3-256 signature) (`pdf-go-blch`)
- `SignOptions.PAdES bool` — emit an ETSI.CAdES.detached (PAdES baseline) signature: `/SubFilter /ETSI.CAdES.detached` + the ESS signing-certificate-v2 signed attribute (RFC 5035, `oidAttrSigningCertV2`)
- `SignOptions.Certify CertifyPermission` (`NotCertified`/`CertifyNoChanges`/`CertifyFillForms`/`CertifyAnnotations`, mirroring Aspose `DocMDPAccessPermissions`) — a certification (author/DocMDP) signature: the `/Sig` dict gets a `/Reference` with `/TransformMethod /DocMDP` + `/TransformParams /P`, and the catalog `/Perms/DocMDP` points at the signature. pyHanko reports `docmdp_ok`
- `SignOptions.TimestampURL string` — fetch an RFC 3161 timestamp from that TSA over the signature value and embed it as the signature-time-stamp **unsigned** attribute ([1] IMPLICIT SET), anchoring the time to a trusted clock (`pkcs7_timestamp.go`: `buildTimestampRequest` → POST `application/timestamp-query` → parse `TimeStampResp` → `marshalTimestampUnsignedAttr`). Validated end-to-end against DigiCert's production TSA; pyHanko reports `TIMESTAMP_TOKEN<INTACT:TRUSTED>`. Requires network at sign time
- `SignOptions.Incremental bool` + **multiple signatures** (`sign_incremental.go`) — signing writes an incremental update (the original bytes verbatim + an appended revision: new/modified objects, a classic xref section with `/Prev` → the previous one, a fresh trailer carrying the original `/ID`) instead of rewriting, so any earlier signature stays valid. Auto-enabled when the document already has a signature; requires a document opened from an existing PDF. Capture at open (`document.go`): `catalogNum` (`/Root`), `docID` (`/ID`), `origSize` (`/Size`), `encryptObjNum` (`/Encrypt`) — new objects start at `origSize` (the stripped `/Pages`/`/Catalog` numbers still occupy slots in the file). `buildIncrementalSignedPDF` adds the Sig dict + Sig field/widget (`uniqueSignatureFieldName` → `Signature1`, `Signature2`, …), modifies `/AcroForm/Fields` + the page `/Annots` + (for DocMDP/new AcroForm) the catalog in place by original number, then `applySignature` patches the placeholders. Validated with pyHanko: first signature `ENTIRE_REVISION` + `ACCEPTABLE_MODIFICATIONS`, second `ENTIRE_FILE` `UNTOUCHED`
- **Signing encrypted documents** — an encrypted document is always signed incrementally: the appended signature objects are encrypted with the document's own scheme (RC4-128 / AES-128 / AES-256) while the signature `/Contents` and `/ByteRange` stay plaintext (written as `pdfRaw`, per ISO 32000-1 §7.6.2). The reader side exempts a signature dict's `/Contents` from decryption (`isSignatureDict` in `decrypt.go`, applied across the RC4/AES-128/AES-256 decrypt walkers). A freshly-built encrypted document (no source) is signed by `buildFreshEncryptedSignedPDF`: serialize the encrypted PDF, reopen it (so it has source + preserved encryption), then sign incrementally — the only form pyHanko/Acrobat accept (full-rewrite-then-sign confuses revision-aware validators). The incremental trailer repeats `/Encrypt`. Validated with pyHanko across all three algorithms: `INTACT:TRUSTED,UNTOUCHED`, `ENTIRE_FILE`
- Visible signature: `SignOptions.Visible` + `Rect Rectangle` + `Page int` (mirrors Aspose `Sign(..., visible, rect, page)`) draw a generated appearance block ("Digitally signed by …", date, optional reason/location) via `generateSignatureAppearance` (`appearance_sign.go`) → an `/AP/N` Form XObject drawn with a Standard-14 font (so the built-in renderer shows it). `SignOptions.Appearance *SignatureAppearance` customizes content/style (`ShowName`/`ShowDate`/`ShowReason`/`ShowLocation`/`Font`/`FontSize`/`Color`; nil = full default block) — mirrors Aspose's `SignatureCustomAppearance`. The appearance does not affect the CMS (it is part of the signed bytes, written before the signature is computed)
- `(*Document).VerifySignatures() ([]SignatureVerification, error)` — verifies every `/Sig` field against the document's source bytes (stored on Open in `d.source`). `SignatureVerification` — `FieldName`, `SignerName`, `Reason`, `Location`, `SigningTime`, `Valid`, `IntegrityOK`, `CoversWholeDocument`, `Certificate *x509.Certificate`, `Chain []*x509.Certificate` (the other certificates the signer embedded — the intermediates needed to build a path; the signer is not repeated), `Err`. Trust-chain validation is the caller's (the certificates are returned)
- `(*Document).SignatureNames() []string` and `(*Document).VerifySignature(fieldName string) (SignatureVerification, error)` (`pdf-go-w3i5`) — mirror Aspose.PDF for .NET's `GetSignatureNames` and `VerifySignature(sigName)`. The error reports a missing field or missing source bytes; a signature that is present but invalid is not an error — it comes back in the result with the reason in `Err`, which is also why Aspose's throwing/non-throwing `VerifySignature`/`TryVerifySignature` pair collapses into one method here
- **Revocation and LTV** (`ocsp.go` / `crl.go` / `revocation.go` / `dss.go`, epic `pdf-go-x2s6`; design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-signature-revocation-ltv-design.md`): `VerifySignatures`/`VerifySignature` take `ValidationOptions{Revocation, Fetcher, Timeout}` — `RevocationNone` (zero value) checks nothing, `RevocationOffline` uses only material the document carries (its `/DSS`), `RevocationOnline` also fetches from the certificate's OCSP responders and CRL distribution points. The result gains `Revocation *RevocationStatus{Status, Source, RevokedAt, Reason, ProducedAt, Err}` and `LTVEnabled bool` (the `/DSS` carries certificates plus a verifying revocation answer for this signer; mirrors Aspose's `IsLtvEnabled`). **`Valid` keeps its cryptographic meaning** — a revoked certificate never flips it. OCSP is hand-rolled on `encoding/asn1` (`buildOCSPRequest`, `parseOCSPResponse`, `parseOCSPAny` — which also accepts the bare `BasicOCSPResponse` a `/DSS /OCSPs` entry holds —, `verifyOCSPResponse`): a response counts only when signed by the issuer or by a delegated responder the issuer signed carrying `id-kp-OCSPSigning`, and an expired/future-dated answer or one about another certificate is never a "good". OpenSSL (`ocsp -reqin -req_text`) parses our requests. CRLs go through `x509.ParseRevocationList` plus issuer-signature and freshness checks (`checkCRL`). Fetching is behind `RevocationFetcher` (built-in transport: `DefaultRevocationFetcher`, 10 MB response cap), which is how tests stay offline. The issuer is found among the signature's embedded certificates (`issuerOf`). `(*Document).AddValidationInfo(opts...)` writes `/DSS` (`/Certs` `/OCSPs` `/CRLs` + `/VRI` keyed by the uppercase SHA-1 of the signature's `/Contents` octets) and `/Extensions /ADBE /ExtensionLevel 5` as **a new revision** through `appendRevision` — the revision writer now shared with incremental signing — and marks the document `revisionAppended`, so `WriteTo` emits those bytes verbatim instead of rebuilding. `SignOptions.LTV` signs, reopens and runs `AddValidationInfo` with `RevocationOnline` (`buildSignedWithLTV`). No independent `/DSS` validator is available locally (pyHanko absent). Out of scope: building a path to a trust anchor, document timestamps (PAdES B-LTA), OCSP nonces, delta/indirect CRLs
- The byte-range dance (`sign.go`): the writer emits fixed-width `pdfRaw` placeholders for `/Contents` (`<` + 16384 zero hex + `>`) and `/ByteRange` (`[0 0000000000 …]`); `buildSignatureObjects` adds the `/Sig` dict + invisible Sig field/widget (`Rect [0 0 0 0]`) into `/AcroForm/Fields` with `/SigFlags 3`; after serialization `applySignature` finds the placeholders, fills the real `/ByteRange` (the excluded gap is the whole `/Contents` value **including the `<>` brackets** — the convention validators expect), hashes the covered bytes, builds the PKCS#7, and splices the hex in-place without shifting offsets
- CMS is hand-rolled on `encoding/asn1` (stdlib has no PKCS#7): `buildPKCS7Detached` (SignedData with contentType/messageDigest/signingTime signed attributes; signature over the SET-OF-re-tagged attrs) and `verifyPKCS7Detached` (parse, recover signer cert by issuer+serial, check messageDigest against the hash the SignerInfo names, verify RSA PKCS#1v1.5 / ECDSA). Validated against **OpenSSL** (`cms -verify`) and **pyHanko** (`INTACT:TRUSTED,UNTOUCHED`, coverage `ENTIRE_FILE`) — invisible, visible, PAdES, DocMDP, RFC 3161-timestamped, multi-signature, and encrypted-document alike. Out of scope: image/logo in the appearance
- Test certs are generated in-memory (`crypto/x509`); **no private key is ever committed** (avoids secret-scanner findings)

QR's Reed-Solomon and mask selection are fully algorithmic (GF(256) arithmetic + generator-polynomial construction from the single primitive-polynomial constant, no per-version EC table beyond the block-size table ISO 18004 requires); validated by an independent self-decoder in `barcode_qr_test.go` that recomputes function-pattern geometry from the version, extracts and unmasks the format info, reads codewords back in zigzag order, and asserts each block's Reed-Solomon syndromes are all zero. This machinery caught a real generator-polynomial index bug (the `x` and `root` terms swapped between `qrRSGeneratorPoly`'s two accumulators) during development — but a second, more subtle bug (`writeFormatInfo`'s module coordinates fully transposed, row/col swapped, except the two positions a transpose can't move) passed every test at first, because the self-decoder's format-info reader was written by mirroring the writer's code rather than independently: a self-mirroring reader agrees with a wrong writer by construction. Code review caught it; a from-scratch decoder built against a reference implementation's verbatim source (fetched and hand-translated from its `(x, y)` = (column, row) convention to this codebase's `(row, col)` one) confirmed it and pinned the fix, and the self-decoder's format-info extraction was then rewritten from that same source rather than from `writeFormatInfo`'s code, closing the blind spot. Lesson generalized: a round-trip self-test only proves two independently-*derived* implementations agree, not that either matches the spec — mirroring one side's code into the other's "independent" checker defeats the whole point. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `BarcodeField`/`Symbology`. **Third-party decoder harness** (`tools/validate_barcodes.py` + `_examples/barcode_verify`): renders 17 symbols of all three symbologies — every printable ASCII character in Code128, QR versions with multi-block and version-info areas plus UTF-8, PDF417 including the 1,108-byte capacity edge — through the real field → appearance → rasterizer pipeline and has **zxing-cpp** (`pip install zxing-cpp pillow`) read the pixels back; all 17 decode byte-for-byte. This closes what was earlier written down as a residual risk (Code128's hand-recalled pattern table, and QR/Code128 never having met a real reader) — a real decoder *was* obtainable offline via pip all along, so the earlier "no reference decoder available" reasoning, including for the QR and Code128 limits above, was too pessimistic. Run it after touching any encoder or the barcode appearance code. **`BarcodePDF417`** (`barcode_pdf417.go` / `barcode_pdf417_tables.go` / `tools/genpdf417`, `pdf-go-cyzm`, ISO/IEC 15438): byte compaction only — the raw UTF-8 bytes (latch 901, or 924 when the count is a multiple of 6; every six bytes packed into five base-900 codewords), preceded by an ECI 000026 (UTF-8) designator when any byte is non-ASCII; text/numeric compaction are size optimisations, not capabilities. The hard part — the 2,787-entry (929 codewords × 3 clusters) codeword-to-bar-pattern table (ISO 15438 Annex A) — was originally judged un-transcribable by hand, so it is **never transcribed**: `tools/genpdf417` (build-tagged `ignore`) parses it mechanically out of a downloaded copy of ZXing's `PDF417.java`, and it was then matched entry-for-entry against zint's independently developed copy (all 2,787 identical) and structurally verified by `TestPDF417TableStructure` (17 modules, four bars + four spaces of width 1-6, cluster value `(b1-b2+b3-b4) mod 9` = 0/3/6 per cluster, no duplicates, ISO start `8-1-1-1-1-1-1-3` / stop `7-1-1-3-1-1-1-2-1`). The table is Apache-2.0 data from ZXing — attribution in `third_party/PDF417-TABLE-NOTICE.txt` + README. Everything else is computed: Reed-Solomon over GF(929) uses a generator built from its roots 3^1..3^k (`pdf417Generator`, pinned to ISO Annex F Tables F.1-F.5 in `TestPDF417GeneratorMatchesISO`, checked algebraically — monic, roots 3^1..3^k — for all nine levels in `TestPDF417GeneratorRoots`, and compared once against zint's table for all nine); the security level follows ISO's recommendation for the data size (2/3/4/5, lowered only if the symbol would not otherwise fit); dimensions follow Annex Q (`pdf417Rows`). The column count is chosen so the rendered symbol (rows drawn 3 modules tall) approaches the **widget rectangle's proportions** — `renderBarcodeModules` gained an `aspect` parameter for this (validation callers pass 0; whether a value fits never depends on it), and `barcodeModules.Square` became `Uniform` (module aspect preserved, scaled to fit and centred — QR and PDF417; Code128 stretches). Capacity ~1,100 bytes (at most 929 codewords per symbol, `cols×rows ≤ 929` — `TestPDF417Capacity` caught a 30×31 = 930-codeword layout that overflowed the table). Validated by an independent test decoder (`decodePDF417Modules`) written from the reference decoder's semantics, not from the encoder — the lesson from the QR format-info bug applied up front: it finds the symbol, checks start/stop per row, reads each codeword back with cluster required to be `row mod 3`, interprets the left/right row indicators as a reader does (row number, column count, row count, security level; all must agree across every row and with the geometry), checks the symbol length descriptor, evaluates the whole codeword polynomial at 3^1..3^k for zero syndromes, and decodes byte compaction with a port of the reference decoder's `byteCompaction`. Then an independent code reviewer decoded 151 generated PDF417 symbols with zxing-cpp and found a few edge cases (a 1,107-byte value wrongly rejected because 929 codewords is prime and so has no rows×columns layout; NaN/∞ aspect; the copyright quote in the notice), all fixed and pinned by hard-coded-literal tests — every one of the seven review mutants (thresholds, level fall-back, pad codeword, drawing orientation, the 929 cap) now fails a test
