- **Diff** (`comparison_diff.go`): common prefix/suffix trimmed; when trimming empties one side, the answer is immediate (one run of deletions or insertions — no search needed), otherwise Myers O(ND) runs over the word keys with the frontier snapshots walked back into an edit script; adjacent same-kind edits group into runs (broken at page changes, rectangles unioned per line). `maxEditDistance` (2000) caps the search — the cost grows with the square of the edit distance in both time and memory (the frontier snapshots, roughly 64 MB at the cap) — beyond it the comparer reports the whole source deleted and the whole destination inserted rather than grinding through, and allocating, the full square
- **Markup** (`comparison_markup.go`): `SaveMarkup`/`WriteMarkup` copy one side (serialize + reopen, so the caller's documents are untouched, and the output is a new document — signatures on the input do not survive the copy) and annotate it — destination side: insertions as `HighlightAnnotation` over the run's rectangles, deletions as a `CaretAnnotation` anchored between the neighbouring unchanged words with the removed text in `/Contents`; source side: deletions as `StrikeOutAnnotation`, insertions as carets. All carry `/T` (default `"Comparison"`), so a viewer's comments panel is the change list. The annotations draw their own appearance streams (`appearance_markup.go`), so the markup paints in our own renderer as well as in Acrobat. `DiffMarkupOptions{Side, InsertColor, DeleteColor, Title, Flatten}` (named apart from `MarkupSection`/`MarkupParagraph`/`PageMarkup` in `paragraph.go`, an unrelated namespace). Marking up an encrypted document is not supported — a document configured for encryption re-encrypts on the copy's `WriteTo`, so reopening it would fail with a bare `ErrEncrypted`; `copyDocument` detects this via `(*Document).Permissions()` and reports it with a wrapped `ErrEncrypted` instead
- Out of scope in phase 1: graphical (pixel) comparison, side-by-side output (shipped in phase 2, below), the HTML/JSON/Markdown diff generators and the Aspose-style generated text report (shipped in phase 3, `comparison_output*.go` below), character-level refinement inside a changed word, and de-hyphenation (a word broken across lines compares as two words)

**`comparison_graphical.go`** — graphical (pixel) comparison, phase 2 of the comparison epic (`pdf-go-175w`/`pdf-go-dyu9`). Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Aspose.Pdf.Comparison.GraphicalComparison` namespace (`GraphicalPdfComparer`, `ImagesDifference`) — for changes the word-level comparer above can't see (moved/edited graphics, font substitution, a replaced scanned image); use the text comparer for text, this one only for graphical changes
- `GraphicalPdfComparer{Threshold, Color, Resolution}` — `NewGraphicalPdfComparer()` gives Aspose's defaults (exact comparison, red, 150 DPI); the zero value works too (`dpi()`/`color()`/`threshold()` fall back the same way — `threshold()` also clamps a negative `Threshold` to 0, since `distance > threshold` would otherwise flag identical pixels too). `GetDifference(page1, page2) (*ImagesDifference, error)` rasterizes both pages (`RenderImage`) and diffs pixels; `ComparePagesToImage(page1, page2, path)` / `WritePagesToImage(..., w)` save `DifferenceToImage` as a PNG; `CompareDocumentsToPdf(doc1, doc2, path)` / `WriteDocumentsToPdf(..., w)` pair every page by index (mirroring `CompareDocumentsPageByPage`'s pairing; a document missing a page compares that page against a blank white canvas rather than erroring — a page that is itself mostly white then reports a correspondingly small ratio despite being a genuine page-count change) and write one report page per pair — the difference image full-page plus a caption with the ratio
- `ImagesDifference{}` (opaque) — `SourceImage()`/`DestinationImage()` (Mirrors `SourceImage`/`GetDestinationImage`; both padded with white to the two renders' union bounding box, so mismatched page sizes compare cleanly instead of panicking), `DifferenceToImage(foreground, background Color) image.Image` (Mirrors `ImagesDifference.DifferenceToImage`), `DifferentPixels()`/`TotalPixels()`/`Ratio()`/`HasDifferences()` — this library's addition (the bd ticket's own goal: "difference image plus the changed-pixel ratio"); Aspose instead exposes the raw LockBits-style `Difference`/`Height`/`Stride`, a .NET `Bitmap` implementation detail with no Go equivalent worth mirroring literally when `image.Image` already carries that shape
- `Threshold` (0-100, percentage of the max per-pixel channel-sum distance 765) makes a small colour change — recompression noise, anti-aliasing — not count as different; validated directly (a controlled ~1.3%-distance colour change is caught at `Threshold: 0` and ignored at `Threshold: 50`)

**`comparison_sidebyside.go`** — side-by-side comparison, phase 2 of the comparison epic. Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `SideBySidePdfComparer`: a two-column "before / after" spread with the differences highlighted — built entirely on phase-1 machinery (`comparison.go`'s word diff, `comparison_markup.go`'s `WriteMarkup`) plus `PdfPageStamp` (`stamp_pdfpage.go`) to place each pane, so unlike Aspose's rasterized output the spread stays **vector** — each pane is the real page content, not a picture of it
- `SideBySideComparePages(page1, page2, outputPath, opts...) (*SideBySidePagesComparisonResult, error)` / `WriteSideBySidePages(..., w, opts...)` and `SideBySideCompareDocuments(doc1, doc2, outputPath, opts...) (*SideBySideDocsComparisonResult, error)` / `WriteSideBySideDocuments(..., w, opts...)` — mirror `SideBySidePdfComparer.Compare(Page/Document, …)`, split into named functions since Go has no overloading (the same adaptation phase 1 already made for `TextPdfComparer`'s static methods). The page variant extracts each page into its own one-page document (`Document.Extract`) so it can reuse `CompareDocumentsPageByPage` + `WriteMarkup` unchanged; the document variant runs those directly. `SideBySideDocsComparisonResult` embeds `*ComparisonResult` (so `Statistics`/`Operations`/`PageOperations` all apply to the spread's own comparison); `SideBySidePagesComparisonResult` wraps the page pair's `[]DiffOperation`
- `SideBySideComparisonOptions{ComparisonOptions, InsertColor, DeleteColor}` — embeds phase 1's options (`ExtractionArea`/`ExcludeAreas1-2`/`ExcludeTables`/`EditOperationsOrder`/`IgnoreCase` all apply, since the spread is the same word-diff engine). Mirrors Aspose's `SideBySideComparisonOptions` minus `ComparisonMode` (this library's tokenizer already splits on whitespace — behaviour already matches Aspose's `IgnoreSpaces` default; the `Normal`/`ParseSpaces` whitespace-sensitivity distinction is out of scope) and `AdditionalChangeMarks` (margin change bars — out of scope)
- Mechanics: mark up the source side (deletions struck through) and destination side (insertions highlighted) as two independent copies via `WriteMarkup`, reopen both, then for every paired page number stamp the source page into the left half and the destination page into the right half of one output page sized to fit both at their native size, with "Before"/"After" captions. **`DiffMarkupOptions.Flatten: true` is required, not cosmetic**: `PdfPageStamp` places a page via `importPageAsXObject`, which captures only a page's content stream and `/Resources` — never `/Annots` (`imposition.go`) — so without flattening, the highlight/strikeout/caret markup `WriteMarkup` draws as real annotations would be silently dropped the instant the marked-up page is stamped as a Form XObject. Found by reasoning through the mechanism before writing any test, then pinned by two regression tests: one exercises the un-flattened path directly and confirms the annotation is gone once stamped (`TestSideBySideFlattenIsRequired`), the other renders the finished spread and checks for the actual highlight-green/strikeout-red pixels in each pane (`TestSideBySideMarkupIsVisible`) — the word-presence-only assertion in the main test does *not* catch a dropped `Flatten`, since `AddText`'s glyphs are page content independent of any annotation and would survive the Form-XObject placement either way; confirmed by temporarily reverting the fix and rerunning the suite during development, which only the pixel-level test failed on

**`comparison_output.go` / `comparison_output_html.go` / `comparison_output_json.go` / `comparison_output_markdown.go` / `comparison_output_pdf.go`** — diff output generators, phase 3 of the comparison epic (`pdf-go-175w`/`pdf-go-9sig`). Mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Aspose.Pdf.Comparison.OutputGenerator` namespace: `IStringOutputGenerator`/`IFileOutputGenerator`, `HtmlDiffOutputGenerator`, `JsonDiffOutputGenerator`, `MarkdownDiffOutputGenerator`, `PdfOutputGenerator` — pure serializers over the phase-1 `DiffOperation` model, distinct from `comparison_markup.go`'s annotation-based markup
- Aspose overloads `GenerateOutput` on the argument shape: a single `List<DiffOperation>` (what `ComparePages` returns) versus a `List<List<DiffOperation>>` (what `CompareDocumentsPageByPage`/`CompareFlatDocuments` return directly, one page's ops per inner list) that additionally renders a "Page N" section per entry. Go has no overloading, so these become distinct method names — `GenerateOutput`/`SaveOutput`/`WriteOutput` for the flat shape, `GenerateOutputPages`/`SaveOutputPages`/`WriteOutputPages` for the per-page shape — mirrored as two real Go interfaces: `StringDiffOutputGenerator{GenerateOutput, GenerateOutputPages}` (mirrors `IStringOutputGenerator`) and `FileDiffOutputGenerator{SaveOutput, SaveOutputPages, WriteOutput, WriteOutputPages}` (mirrors `IFileOutputGenerator`; the `io.Writer` pair is this library's addition, following the `SaveXxx`/`WriteXxx` convention used throughout). `(*ComparisonResult).Pages() [][]DiffOperation` is the missing link — the per-page shape as a method, since Aspose's comparer methods return that shape directly while this library's return a richer `*ComparisonResult`; in page-by-page mode it is the result's own per-page storage, in flat mode it's built from `PageOperations` up to the highest page number any operation touches
- `DiffOutputStyle{InsertColor, InsertBackground, DeleteColor, DeleteBackground, EqualColor, EqualBackground *Color; StrikethroughDelete bool}` — mirrors the intent of `OutputTextStyle`'s three `TextStyle{Color, BackgroundColor}` pairs, flattened into one struct since `TextStyle` already names an unrelated type in this library. Zero value resolves to the same green/red pair `DiffMarkupOptions` defaults to (`DiffOutputStyle.resolved()`), keeping every comparison output visually consistent; `EqualColor`/`EqualBackground` default to nil (plain/unstyled equal text). Consumed by `HTMLDiffOutputGenerator`/`PDFDiffOutputGenerator` (`NewXxx(opts ...DiffOutputStyle)`, last one wins); `JSONDiffOutputGenerator`/`MarkdownDiffOutputGenerator` take no style at all — parameterless constructors, exactly matching Aspose (JSON has no visual concept to style, and Markdown's own syntax already fixes how insert/delete are marked)
- **HTML** (`comparison_output_html.go`): renders an HTML *fragment* (colored `<span style="...">`, inline CSS from `DiffOutputStyle`, no `<html>`/`<head>` boilerplate), meant for embedding into the caller's own page or email — matching `IStringOutputGenerator`'s "generate a string" intent, as opposed to `SaveHTML`'s self-contained-document export elsewhere in this library. Equal text is emitted plain (unescaped by a wrapping span) unless `EqualColor`/`EqualBackground` is set; `StrikethroughDelete` adds `text-decoration:line-through` to deletions only. `GenerateOutputPages` wraps each page in `<div class="cmp-page" data-page="N"><h3>Page N</h3>…</div>`. Text is HTML-escaped (`html.EscapeString`); operations are joined by a literal space, matching `AssembleSourceText`/`AssembleDestinationText`'s own join convention
- **JSON** (`comparison_output_json.go`): a flat JSON array of `{"operation","text","sourcePage","destPage","sourceRects","destRects"}` objects (rects are this library's addition over Aspose's own `DiffOperation`, matching `comparison.go`'s own note that the rectangle fields are ours); `GenerateOutputPages` wraps that array as `[{"page":N,"operations":[...]}]`. Rectangles get their own lowerCamelCase `{llx,lly,urx,ury}` shape (`diffRectJSON`, a direct field-layout-preserving type conversion from `Rectangle` — `Rectangle` itself carries no `json` tags, being a shared type used well beyond JSON output)
- **Markdown** (`comparison_output_markdown.go`): `**inserted**` (bold) / `~~deleted~~` (GFM strikethrough) / plain equal text, escaped through the existing `mdEscapeText` (`markdown_export.go`). No style options at all, matching Aspose's parameterless constructor — GFM strikethrough is the only way Markdown can represent a deletion, so `StrikethroughDelete` has no Markdown equivalent to toggle. `GenerateOutputPages` adds a `## Page N` heading per section
- **PDF report** (`comparison_output_pdf.go`, `PDFDiffOutputGenerator`/`PDFDiffReportOptions{DiffOutputStyle, Format, Title}`) — the one generator that implements only `FileDiffOutputGenerator` (a PDF cannot be a string, matching Aspose: `PdfOutputGenerator` does not implement `IStringOutputGenerator` either). Built through this library's Flow layer, per the bd ticket's own framing — but not through the public `(*Flow).AddParagraph` (one `TextStyle` per whole paragraph, no per-word color), through the internal styled-runs engine `flow_runs.go` already uses to color bold/italic/link spans inline for the Markdown-to-PDF renderer: each `DiffOperation` becomes one `textRun` colored via `DiffOutputStyle.colorFor`, with a leading space prepended to every run after the first (`diffRuns`) — without it, the last word of one operation and the first word of the next would fuse into one unbreakable layout cluster, since `flow_runs.go`'s tokenizer only breaks clusters at an actual space token. `GenerateOutputPages`'s equivalent (`WriteOutputPages`/`SaveOutputPages`) adds an `AddHeading(2, "Page N", …)` before each page's runs; an empty page's operations are a no-op (`flowRunsIndent` already handles zero runs). Verified with the same pixel-level rigor as `comparison_sidebyside.go`'s markup test (`TestPDFDiffOutputGeneratorRendersColors`, mutation-tested by temporarily dropping the `colorFor` call and confirming the test fails) rather than trusting that the inserted/deleted words merely being present proves the coloring survived

**`flow.go`** — flow / document-generator layout (epic `pdf-go-m9kt`, Tier 1): the **flow counterpart to the Rectangle-based drawing API** — content is laid out top-to-bottom and paginated automatically, instead of positioned absolutely. An additive layer (it computes Rectangles and calls the existing `AddText`/`AddImage`/`AddTable`/`drawList`), so it coexists with the Rectangle paradigm. Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's generator / `Page.Paragraphs` flow model
- `(*Document).NewFlow(opts FlowOptions) *Flow` — `FlowOptions{Format, Margin{Left,Right,Top,Bottom} (zero → 54pt), ParagraphSpacing (zero → 6pt), Tagged *TaggedContent}`. Builders (chainable): `AddParagraph`, `AddHeading(level, …)`, `AddImage(path, w, h)` / `AddImageAlt(…, alt)` (h ≤ 0 → preserve aspect via `image.DecodeConfig`), `AddTable(*Table)`, `AddList(items, ordered, style)`, `AddSpacer(h)`. `Render() (pages int, error)` lays everything out and returns the page span
- Engine: a `flowState` cursor (current page + Y) over a content box (page minus margins). `startPage` reuses the document's initial blank page (resized) when it has exactly one with no content, else appends. Paragraphs/headings **split across pages line-by-line** (`wrapText` → draw the lines that fit, new page, continue); images are atomic (scaled down to one content area if oversized); tables draw inline when they fit, on a fresh page otherwise, and fall back to `AddTable`'s own pagination when taller than a page; lists use the shared `drawList`. When `Tagged` is set, each element is auto-tagged (`/P`, `/H1…/H6`, `/Figure`+`/Alt`, `AddTaggedTable`, tagged `drawList`) so the flow output passes `ValidatePDFUA` — a one-call accessible report generator
- **Floating boxes** (`flow_box.go`, Tier 2): `FloatingBox` is a positioned content container with an optional border/background/padding holding its own content (`NewFloatingBox().AddParagraph/AddHeading/AddImage/AddList/AddSpacer().SetBorder/SetBackground/SetPadding/SetSpacing`). `SetSpacing(gap)` overrides the inter-element gap (default 6pt; `0` for a single-paragraph box so symmetric padding centres it vertically). The border honours `BorderInfo.Sides` — a single side renders as a rule (e.g. `BorderSideLeft` for a block-quote) rather than a full outline (`drawBoxFrame` draws per-side edges, only `BorderSideAll` strokes the whole rect). `(*Page).AddFloatingBox(box, rect)` places it absolutely (paints the frame, flows content within `rect`−padding, clips on overflow); `(*Flow).AddFloatingBox(box)` inserts it in the flow at its **measured** height (`measureFlowElems`; new page if it doesn't fit). The box lays out via a `boxed` `flowState` (`newPage` → `errBoxFull` stops instead of paginating) reusing all element drawing; when the document is tagged the box is a `/Div` (content tagged under it via the new `flowState.parent`) and its frame an `/Artifact`. Tables are not allowed inside a box (they paginate)
- **Multi-column layout** (Tier 3): `FlowOptions.Columns` (>1) + `ColumnGap` (zero → 18pt) divide the content box into N columns; the engine fills a column top-to-bottom then moves to the next via `flowState.advance` (column → next column → next page), with `colLeft()` giving the current column's X and `contentW` the per-column width. `(*Flow).AddColumnBreak()` forces the following content into the next column (or, from the last column, the next page) — used to put one section per column. Works with tagging (content stays under the structure tree across columns) and pagination; tables/boxes flow within the current column (a wide table in a narrow column overflows — use a single column for those). Boxed (`FloatingBox`) layout stays single-column (`advance` → `errBoxFull`)
- **Text flow-around** (`flow_float.go`, Tier 3): `(*Flow).AddFloatBox(box, FloatLeft|FloatRight, width)` draws a `FloatingBox` pinned to a column edge and registers an `activeFloat` band; the following paragraphs wrap **line by line** around it (`flowText` → `flowTextAround` when `len(floats) > 0`): each line's `[left,right]` comes from `lineBounds(y)` (column minus any active float band + `floatTextGap`), `nextLine` greedily fits words into that width, lines on one page are bracketed into a single tagged `/P` (`flush`), and the cursor returns to full width once it passes the float's `bottom` (`pruneFloats`). A line with no room beside the float drops to `nextFloatBottom`; non-wrapping elements (image/table/list/box) call `dropBelowFloats` to start on a clean line below the float. Floats are cleared on a column/page break (so they don't span pages). Designed for single-column flows; in a multi-column flow the box floats within the current column
- Tier-3 remaining (not yet): keep-with-next / widow-orphan control, image floats (only boxes float), splitting a single paragraph's tagging into one `/P` across pages (currently one `/P` per page-chunk)

**`validate.go`**
- `Validate(inputPath)` — checks a PDF for **structural integrity** (parseable + internally consistent); returns `*ValidationReport` with a `Valid` flag and a list of `ValidationIssue` (code + message). NOT a standards check: it does not validate PDF/A or PDF/UA. This differs from Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.Validate`, which checks PDF/A·PDF/UA conformance — the capability here is intentionally narrower
- Issue codes: `INVALID_HEADER`, `XREF_ERROR`, `OBJECT_ERROR`, `PAGE_TREE_ERROR`, `STREAM_ERROR`, `ENCRYPTED`
- Checks performed: header, xref/trailer, all objects readable, page tree traversal, orphaned `/Pages` nodes, `/Page` → `/Parent` refs resolve to `/Pages`, streams without `/Filter` don't contain compressed data, image XObjects declare the required `/ColorSpace` + `/BitsPerComponent` (ISO 32000-1 §8.9.5; image masks and JPXDecode images exempt — `validateImageXObjects`). Rendering stays tolerant where Acrobat refuses; the check is Acrobat-compatibility diagnostics only

**`validate_pdfa.go`** — PDF/A archival-conformance validator (epic `pdf-go-s2n`, phase 1). Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.Validate(PdfFormat)` but returns a structured report instead of an XML log
- `(*Document).ValidatePDFA(format PDFAFormat) *PDFAValidationReport` — read-only diagnostic (never mutates); the write-side counterpart is `ConvertToPDFA` (`pdfa_convert.go`, below)
- `PDFAFormat` enum — both conformance levels: `PDFA1B`/`PDFA2B`/`PDFA3B` (basic) and `PDFA1A`/`PDFA2A`/`PDFA3A` (accessible). `part()` → 1/2/3; `conformance()` → `"A"`/`"B"`. The **"a"** levels add the Tagged-PDF requirement: `pdfaCheckTagged` (run only for `conformance()=="A"`) flags `NOT_TAGGED` (`/MarkInfo /Marked`), `NO_STRUCT_TREE` (`/StructTreeRoot`) and `NO_LANG` (`/Catalog/Lang`) — author the structure tree with `(*Document).TaggedContent` (`tagged.go`). The XMP check matches `pdfaid:conformance` against the requested letter
- `PDFAValidationReport` struct — `Format`, `Conformant bool`, `Issues []PDFAIssue`; `PDFAIssue` — `Rule` (stable code) + `Message`
- Rules + codes: `XMP_MISSING`/`XMP_PDFAID_MISSING`/`XMP_PART_MISMATCH`/`XMP_CONFORMANCE_MISMATCH` (XMP packet with matching `pdfaid:part`/`pdfaid:conformance`, regex-read from `XMPRaw`), `FONT_NOT_EMBEDDED` (every Type1/TrueType/Type0 font **a content stream actually selects with `Tf`** carries `/FontFile`/`/FontFile2`/`/FontFile3`; Type3 is glyph-stream-embedded; CIDFont descendants checked via their Type0 parent). Usage comes from `pdfaUsedFonts` (`pdfa_fonts.go`), which walks every content stream — pages, Form XObjects incl. annotation appearances, Type3 glyph procedures — and resolves each `Tf` name through that stream's resources: PDF/A requires embedding for the fonts used to render (ISO 19005-1 §6.3.4), and a face left in a resource dict (every Acrobat form keeps ZapfDingbats in `/AcroForm/DR`) renders nothing. Checking every font object instead raised a violation veraPDF does not — 130 of 1,009 corpus documents were flagged for a font nothing drew with, `ENCRYPTED`, `JAVASCRIPT`/`LAUNCH_ACTION` (scan `/Names/JavaScript`, `/OpenAction`, and every action dict's `/S`), `COLOR_NO_OUTPUT_INTENT` (a page content stream uses a device-colour operator `rg`/`RG`/`g`/`G`/`k`/`K` but the catalog has no `/OutputIntents` with a `/DestOutputProfile`), `TRANSPARENCY` (PDF/A-1 only, both conformance letters — `pdf-go-o1le` fixed a gate that read `format != PDFA1B` and so silently skipped PDF/A-1a: transparency group, `/SMask` ≠ `/None`, non-Normal `/BM`, or `/ca`/`/CA` < 1), `ANNOTATION_FLAGS`/`ANNOTATION_NO_AP` (Print flag set, Hidden/NoView clear, non-Link visible annots have `/AP`), `METADATA_COMPRESSED` (the `/Metadata` stream is unfiltered), `XMP_MALFORMED` (the packet does not parse as XML), `LZW_FILTER` (PDF/A-1 only, both conformance letters — same `format.part()==1` fix, and previously untested), `EMBEDDED_FILES` (PDF/A-1 only — a `/Names/EmbeddedFiles` entry, a non-empty catalog `/AF`, **or** a page-pinned `FileAttachmentAnnotation` with a file, `pdf-go-tdx5`, since an associated file reaches its bytes through any of the three). Validated on the live in-memory document (Standard-14 fonts flagged, embedded TTF not flagged)

**`pdfa_convert.go`** — PDF/A conformance writer (epic `pdf-go-s2n`, phase 2). Mirrors the intent of Aspose.PDF for .NET's `Document.Convert(PdfFormat)`
- `(*Document).ConvertToPDFA(format PDFAFormat) (*PDFAValidationReport, error)` — applies the structural/metadata fixes the library can make safely in place (mutates the document; `Save`/`WriteTo` writes it) and returns a fresh `ValidatePDFA` report of whatever still fails. When `Conformant` is true the document satisfies the validator's checks
- Transforms: `RemoveEncryption`; strip JavaScript/Launch actions (catalog `/OpenAction`/`/AA`, `/Names/JavaScript`, per-annotation `/A`/`/AA`, then delete the now-orphaned action objects); remove `/Names/EmbeddedFiles`, the catalog `/AF`, and every page-pinned `FileAttachmentAnnotation`'s `/FS` for PDF/A-1 (`pdf-go-tdx5`; the writer sweeps the now-unreachable filespec/stream objects in the same reachability pass); **flatten transparency for PDF/A-1** (`FlattenTransparency`, `flatten_transparency.go`/`pdf-go-bqxs`; PDF/A-1 forbids transparency outright — ISO 19005-1 — while PDF/A-2/-3 permit it, so the call is gated on `format.part()==1` and runs before the font pass below, so a page's now-image-only content doesn't drag its former fonts into `embedStandardFonts`/`embedCompositeFonts` for nothing; `pdf-go-o1le`, closing the last open item of `pdf-go-ovc0`'s point 3 — flattening itself already existed, only the wiring into `ConvertToPDFA` was missing); set annotation `/F` (Print on, Hidden/NoView off); **draw missing annotation appearances** (`generatePDFAAppearances`: form-field widgets through `regenerateWidgetAppearance`, drawing/markup annotations through their own `RegenerateAppearance`; a conforming reader may not synthesize one, so a widget with no `/AP` would vanish) and clear `/AcroForm/NeedAppearances`; **auto-embed the simple fonts the document draws with** (`embedStandardFonts`/`buildEmbeddedSimpleFont`, see below); **embed composite (CJK) fonts as a subset** (`embedCompositeFonts`, `pdfa_fonts.go`); add an sRGB ICC **OutputIntent** (`/S /GTS_PDFA1`, `/DestOutputProfile` → ICC stream); write a `pdfaid` **XMP** packet synced from `/Info` (uncompressed, so it also clears `METADATA_COMPRESSED`)
- **Standard-14 / non-embedded simple-font embedding**: every non-embedded `Type1`/`TrueType`/`MMType1` font is rewritten in place (same object number, so content streams and resource refs are untouched) into an embedded `/Subtype /TrueType` font backed by the **bundled metric-compatible substitute** (`fallbackFontFor`: Arimo↔Helvetica/Arial, Tinos↔Times, Cousine↔Courier, …, the same clones the renderer uses). The original `/Encoding` is preserved and `/Widths` (`/FirstChar` 0 `/LastChar` 255) are computed from the substitute's *own* glyph advances (`ttfFont.glyphID` → `glyphWidths`, scaled to 1000/`unitsPerEm`) so the dictionary and the embedded program agree, as PDF/A requires. Because the clones are metric-compatible, layout and word-wrap are unchanged and text still extracts/renders correctly. `Symbol`/`ZapfDingbats` have no Latin substitute (`fallbackFontFor` returns nil) and stay a reported violation; composite (Type0/CJK) and Type3 fonts are out of scope
- **Accessible ("a") levels**: `ConvertToPDFA(PDFA1A/2A/3A)` runs the same transforms and writes `pdfaid:conformance "A"`, but does not build the structure tree (that is the caller's job via `TaggedContent` — auto-tagging arbitrary content is out of scope). The returned report flags `NOT_TAGGED`/`NO_STRUCT_TREE`/`NO_LANG` when the document was not tagged first. A document authored with `TaggedContent` then converted with `PDFA1A` is fully conformant
- `srgbICCProfile()` builds a minimal but valid **ICC v2.1 RGB display profile** in pure Go (128-byte header with `acsp`/`mntr`/`RGB `/D50 illuminant, tag table, `desc`/`wtpt`/`r,g,bXYZ` sRGB D50-adapted primaries/`r,g,bTRC` gamma-2.2 curves/`cprt`), so no external `.icc` file is bundled. The stream is Flate-compressed by the writer
- **Composite (CJK) font embedding** (`pdfa_fonts.go`): `pdfaUsedCIDs` decodes every show operator through the font's own CMap (predefined CJK encodings yield real CIDs; Identity yields the raw code), and `embedCompositeFonts` subsets the face `fontRepo.findCJK` would render with — a collection sub-font re-wrapped via `standaloneSFNT` first — reaching glyphs as the renderer does (CID → Unicode through the ordering table or `/ToUnicode` → glyph). The rebuilt descendant carries `/FontFile2`, a `/CIDToGIDMap` stream translating the document's CIDs into the subset's glyphs, and `/W` from the subset itself. Only used glyphs are embedded (a whole CJK face is 10-16 MB; a converted corpus document grew 3 KB → 35 KB)
- **Symbol/ZapfDingbats**: no Latin clone carries their glyphs, so `symbolFaceFor` takes a face registered through `AddFontFile`/`AddFontFolder`, else the installed face of the same family (`findSystemFamily` — matching by family, since the installed Symbol's PostScript name is `SymbolMT`). Status: **render epic complete (P1–P6 + annotations + multi-page TIFF)** (vector + images + text + clip/alpha/shadings + annotation appearances + stroke quality → PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/TIFF). Because their advance widths equal the originals, word-wrapped layout is preserved and glyphs aren't distorted; serif/mono and bold/italic render distinctly. `render_fontrepo.go` adds a `FontRepository` (mirrors Aspose.PDF for .NET): `AddFontFolder`/`AddFontFile`/`AddSystemFonts` register sources used before the bundled substitute. Internals (lowercase): `flattener` adaptively flattens Bézier/arc paths to device-space polylines; `rasterizer` produces anti-aliased coverage via analytic-X + 4× supersampled-Y scanlines (nonzero + even-odd); `compositeCoverage` does src-over with an optional clip mask; `strokeToFill` (`raster_stroke.go`) builds the stroke outline with real line caps (butt/round/square), line joins (miter — with miter-limit→bevel fallback — / round / bevel) and dash patterns (`applyDash`); `renderer` interprets the content stream (q/Q/cm/w, path ops, f/S/B painting, Gray/RGB/CMYK colour, text with `Tr` rendering modes — fill/stroke, invisible mode 3 paints nothing, clip modes 4-7 accumulate the shown glyph outlines and intersect them into the graphics-state clip at `ET` (`applyTextClip`, ISO 32000-1 §9.4.3) so the common "show glyphs under `7 Tr`, then paint a full-page image/fill through them" idiom renders as glyph-shaped text, `Do` images, `BI` inline images, `gs`, `W`/`W*` clip, `sh`, `J`/`j`/`M`/`d` stroke params, `cs`/`CS` colour spaces, `BDC`/`EMC` Optional-Content visibility) and **skips the few operators not yet supported** so any page renders. Stencil image masks (`/ImageMask true`, inline `/IM true`, `render_imagemask.go`) paint the current fill colour through their 1-bit "on" samples (per `/Decode`), inverse-mapped through the CTM. A `/JBIG2Decode` image mask is JBIG2-decoded first (its globals come from `/DecodeParms`, which `decodeStream` can't reach), since otherwise the raw compressed bytes would be painted as the mask. Blend modes (`render_blend.go`) are honored: `gs` `/BM` selects a `blendMode` on the graphics state — separable (Multiply/Screen/Overlay/Darken/Lighten/ColorDodge/ColorBurn/HardLight/SoftLight/Difference/Exclusion, per channel) or non-separable (Hue/Saturation/Color/Luminosity, on the whole colour via `Lum`/`Sat`/`SetLum`/`SetSat`/`ClipColor`). The compositors funnel through `blendApply` as `C = (1−a)·Cb + a·B(Cb,Cs)` for an opaque backdrop; Normal/unsupported keep the fast src-over path. Type3 fonts (`render_type3.go`) render each glyph by executing its `/CharProcs` content stream with `FontMatrix · text-rendering matrix · text matrix · CTM`, reusing the interpreter; the code→glyph-name table comes from `/Encoding/Differences`. Optional Content (`render_oc.go`): content tagged with an OCG/OCMD that is OFF in `/Catalog/OCProperties/D` — via a `/OC` marked-content section (`BDC`…`EMC`) or an `/OC` entry on an XObject — is suppressed (OCMD policies AnyOn/AllOn/AnyOff/AllOff honored). After the content stream it paints annotation appearance streams (`render_annotations.go`): every `/Annots` entry's normal appearance (`/AP/N`, selected by `/AS` for state subdictionaries) is drawn as a Form XObject mapped into `/Rect` per ISO 32000-1 §12.5.5 — so AcroForm field widgets, stamps, highlights, free text, etc. render the way a viewer shows them; `/Popup` and Hidden/NoView (`/F` bits 2/6) annotations are skipped. Annotations are drawn in **two passes — non-widgets first, then form-field widgets on top** — mirroring how Acrobat/pdf.js render interactive form fields as a separate top layer (`/Annots` order preserved within each pass); without this a markup annotation later in `/Annots` could hide a field's value (39103.pdf white-outs its baked template text with opaque white `/Square` boxes layered over the placeholder widgets — strict `/Annots` order erased every field). A `/Tx`/`/Ch` widget first gets an opaque background (`/MK/BG`, else white) so baked page content does not show through the field (`widgetFieldBackground`). P5 (`render_clip.go`/`render_gstate.go`/`render_shading.go`): `W`/`W*` clipping intersected into a per-pixel coverage mask (`gs.clip`, applied after the next paint per ISO 32000-1 §8.5.4, saved/restored by q/Q); constant alpha via `gs` → `/ca`/`/CA`/`/LW` (translucent content blends); soft masks via `gs` `/SMask` (`render_softmask.go`): the group `/G` is rendered off-screen and reduced to a per-pixel luminosity/alpha mask that `effectiveClip` folds into every paint (saved/restored by q/Q, cleared by `/None`); axial (type 2) and radial (type 3) shadings via `sh` and shading patterns (PatternType 2), with a m-in/n-out function evaluator (`render_shading.go` + `render_function_ps.go`): types 0 sampled, 2 exponential, 3 stitching, function arrays, and 4 PostScript calculator (a real stack interpreter — arithmetic/stack/comparison/`if`/`ifelse`) and colour model inferred from output-component count. Separation and DeviceN colour spaces (`render_colorspace.go`): `cs`/`CS` resolve the space; on `sc`/`scn` the tint operands run through the tint-transform function (commonly a Type 4) to RGB. Tiling patterns (PatternType 1, `render_tiling.go`) are rendered by executing the cell content stream once per tile across the fill path's bbox (stepped by `/XStep`/`/YStep` through `/Matrix`), clipped to the path ∩ current clip; uncolored (PaintType 2) cells inherit the fill colour set with the pattern; the tile count is capped at `maxTiles`. P6 adds stroke quality (caps/joins/dash above) and the performance pass: `coverageBBox`/`compositeCoverageBBox` allocate and scan only a path's pixel bounding box instead of the whole frame (glyphs/fills are tiny), cutting the 13-page showcase from ~35 s to ~1.1 s at 150 DPI (~30×). `cff.go` adds CFF/Type2 charstring outlines (`pdf-go-l7b`): `parseCFF` reads the CFF container (INDEXes, Top/Private DICTs, charset, FDArray/FDSelect for CID-keyed) and a Type2 interpreter flattens charstrings into the same on-curve `glyphContour` the glyf decoder emits. Embedded OpenType-CFF (`/FontFile3`: Type1C / CIDFontType0C / OpenType) is resolved in `buildRenderFont` via `parseCFFProgram` (bare CFF or `OTTO` wrapper); `.otf` registered in the `FontRepository` is parsed as an sfnt whose `'CFF '` table attaches to `ttfFont.cff`, so `glyphContours` draws from it. `renderFont` carries either `prog` (TrueType) or `cff`; `gid()` maps CID→GID through the CFF charset for CIDFontType0C. **Simple** (non-Type0) CFF fonts (Type1C `/FontFile3`, e.g. MinionPro subsets) build a code→GID map (`cffFont.simpleGID`, `buildSimpleEncoding`): the CFF charset gives GID→SID and the Encoding gives code→glyph — for the predefined Standard encoding a code's SID is `code−31` across 32–126, reversed through the charset; a custom Encoding table (formats 0/1) is read directly. A **predefined** charset (Top DICT charset offset 0 = ISOAdobe) is materialised as the identity GID→SID map so subset fonts that keep the standard glyph order (e.g. NewsGothicBT) still resolve. Without this, simple CFF fonts mapped every code to GID 0 and rendered no text. When the PDF font dict carries its own `/Encoding` (WinAnsi etc.), it **overrides** the font's built-in encoding per ISO 32000-1 §9.6.6.2: the resolved `fi.encoding` rune reaches the glyph through `cffFont.runeToGID` — charset SID → glyph name (`cffStdStrings` 0–390 / String INDEX above) → AGL rune (`cffGlyphNameRune`, incl. uniXXXX/uXXXX) — with the built-in encoding as fallback; subset fonts often embed a built-in encoding covering only a few codes, which previously left pages nearly blank (56333.pdf). The render font cache is keyed by the font's **object number**, not the resource name — a page and a nested Form XObject may both define `/T1_0` pointing at different fonts. (`.otf` embedding via `LoadFont` is now supported — written as `/FontFile3` + `CIDFontType0`, see `embedCFFFont`; this render path draws it back through the same `parseCFFProgram`/`gid()` CFF machinery.) A Type1 charstring interpreter (`t1Interp`: hsbw/sbw, r/h/v-moveto/lineto, rr/hv/vh-curveto, closepath, callsubr/return, div, seac accent composition, and callothersubr flex + hint-replacement via the PS stack) flattens each glyph into the same `glyphContour` the glyf/CFF decoders emit. `renderFont` gains a `t1` program alongside `prog`/`cff`; `gid()` resolves a simple font's code → glyph name (PDF `/Differences` → base-encoding standard name → the font's built-in `/Encoding`) → synthetic GID. The renderer also has a `suppressText` flag (glyph fill/stroke skipped, text-clip accumulation for Tr 4-7 kept) used by the HTML exporter to produce graphics-only backgrounds. Knockout groups (`/K true`) run their sub-renderer with `renderer.knockout`, which routes the vector paint path (fills/strokes/glyphs) through `compositeCoverageKnockout` — within its coverage an element **replaces** the accumulated backdrop (`C' = Cs·a·cov + Cb·(1−cov)`) instead of compositing over it; images inside knockout groups still composite normally (documented limitation). Out of render scope: mesh shadings (ShadingType 4–7), non-embedded Symbol glyph shapes and the rarer decorative ZapfDingbats marks (`pdf-go-ylj`: code→Unicode encoding is wired so embedded/registered fonts render, but no Latin substitute is forced — non-embedded Symbol with no covering font draws nothing rather than .notdef boxes).
